title: Pre-Trained Language Transformers are Universal Image Classifiers

bias_targets.methodology: The paper attempts to mitigate racial and ethnic biases by compiling a balanced dataset from multiple web sources and leveraging the heavy-tail distribution of a Frozen Pre-Trained Transformer (FPT). The authors argue this prevents the model from overfitting to specific demographic features, although they do not provide quantitative evaluations across specific racial or ethnic subgroups.

The authors aim to circumvent gender bias by intentionally sampling images across different genders for a balanced training set and relying on the FPT model's meta-learning capacity. Explicit subgroup parity metrics for gender are not quantitatively reported.

The paper theoretically evaluates and contrasts the architectural inductive bias of traditional Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) with that of pretrained transformers. It argues that CNNs are prone to superficial pattern-matching on imbalanced datasets, whereas FPTs utilize autoregressive pre-training priors to generalize better and avoid this bias.
